artifacts.summary: Nine-phase plan for the positive HitPresented probe on NoFiniteWidth.M at every pre-seam (t, pre m) with Phi' := Phi: seam classification, four letter classes, model-A truncation with an exhibited uniform count windowN m k = min m (card KType + 1), one-gadget presentation, run characterization, by-product presented_node, then WIRED entry and README record.

memory_candidates.content: Seam-fibre finiteness is the discriminator between Presented and HitPresented fixtures in the RaySummary tree. At a seam (t, w) with finitely many histories through it (e.g. NoFiniteWidth's Node.pre m has exactly m + 1, each canonical and eventually constant both ways), a finite presentation realizes the closure traces EXACTLY, so trace-level Presented holds and HitPresented follows for free (hitPresented_of_presented); a Hit-level negative is therefore impossible there, regardless of infinite width or stab-letters in the alphabet. Hit-level falsifiers for requirement (C) must be sought at seams with infinitely many histories through them (model A's (t, a) is the only such fixture in the tree). Corollary for probe design: on a finite-fibre seam the model-A truncation argument buys a count uniform over the seam index, not satisfiability, and such a probe does not test the truncation's necessity.
